Inframetrics Company recommends the following directives when cleaning all 
optical components. The first draft initiated by eng Samy Mohmed Mahmoud 
Bassous Cairo, tested at 10 April 02

items:
All components must be handled in such a way that no foreign matter,
 particularly grease, touches the surface.
Components shall also be protected as much as possible from dust.

Normally the best advise on cleaning optical components is "DONT"
 unless a slightly dirty surface has an appreciable effect on the performance
 of the component. (Any cleaning operation has some associated risk of damage).

Excess dust can often be removed by blowing with clean and dry air. A more
 effective method of removing dust is with compressed gas. The camera must be held
 STRICTLY UPRIGHT to avoid liquid from being released. NEVER blow on the
 components with your breath,

If cleaning becomes necessary, the following materials are recommended:
 a- Clean lens tissue,
 b- Good quality porous cloth,
 c- Micro filter optics cleaner,
 d- Acetone, reagent grade,
 e- Alcohol: This should be 95% pure (190 proof) distilled ethy1 alcohol. Do
 not use 100% pure or 
 "reagent grade", which has the last 5% water
 removed by absorbents. The absorbents leave a residue.
 f- Dispensers for both acetone and alcohol: You must use a dispenser
 designed so that alcohol or acetone 
 dose not return to the main reservoir.
 This is to prevent contamination.

Fold a cotton pad in 1/2 to form a rectangle and then in 1/2 again to
 form a square

Spray optics cleaner directly onto a cotton pad. Using the cotton pad
 "gently" rub surface until it is completely wet
Use another clean and dry cotton pad to wipe component dry

If there still seems to be some grease or dirt on the surface, perform the following
 two steps:
 - Fold a cotton pad as outlined in step 1
 - Dampen (do not saturate) the folded edge with acetone. Starting at the top
 edge of the surface, slowly and gently pull the pad down the surface in one
 motion. You may repeat this several times. If heavy streaks appear, change
 to a clean pad and acetone

Final cleaning follow step 2 except substitute alcohol in place of the
 acetone. The alcohol should remove any small streaks or residue. Repeat if
 necessary
